newsitem.title: USA: US begins process for WTO food equivalency accords.
newsitem.headline: US begins process for WTO food equivalency accords.

text.p: U.S. Food and Drug Administration proposed Wednesday a list of criteria that it plans to use in evaluating whether the food export regulatory systems used by foreign countries are equivalent to those used in the United States.
After evaluating the foreign systems, FDA said it will decide whether to enter into an equivalence agreement with other countries, as allowed under World Trade Organization rules.
In a notice published in the Federal Register, the agency said public comments on the proposed criteria must be received by Aug 4.
FDA expects many of the initial equivalence evaluations to involve fish, because the U.S. imports about 55 percent of the seafood it consumes.
WTO rules allow countries to have different, but equivalent sanitary practices as long as they achieve the same level of food safety protection.

The burden of demonstrating that equivalence exists rests with the exporting country. The importing country has the right to decide for itself whether the regulatory system of the exporting country is equivalent to its own.
Several nations have asked the United States to enter into consultations to develop equivalence agreements for seafood, the FDA said.
In the Federal Register notice, the FDA published a lengthy list of proposed criteria that it wants to use to determine if equivalence exists among trading partners.
